notes: Tests exercise the real code path: a fake IdP (discovery+JWKS, RSA-signed tokens) drives withMCPAuth/oauthSession end-to-end; expired/nbf/other-issuer/typ=ID/cnf/empty-sub/HS256/non-JWT are each refused, off/dormant states change nothing, scope ceiling and token-scope intersection are asserted, and REST/OpenBao surfaces are verified not to accept the token. All Go tests (httpapi, store) and the vitest SettingsPage test pass; go build/vet clean.

Feature is off by default; a fresh install is unaffected. Enabling requires OIDC on with an issuer, enforced both in the UI and in updateSettings (mcp_oauth_requires_oidc). Account lookup is by (issuer, subject) on active OIDC users only — no provisioning, no role from claims. Issuer trailing-slash trimming matches UpsertOIDCUser, so the lookup key is consistent.
go.mod: go-jose/v4 moved from indirect to direct because the test signs tokens with it; go.sum unchanged. Not a scope leak.

internal/httpapi/mcp_oauth.go:106 mcpMetadataURL hardcodes '/.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/mcp' off the origin. If mcp.oauth.resource were set with a path prefix (e.g. https://host/vault/mcp) RFC 9728 would expect /.well-known/oauth-protected-resource/vault/mcp; the server only registers the /mcp variant so it is self-consistent, but such a resource value would not be reachable. Edge case only.

internal/httpapi/mcp_oauth.go:164 a discovery/JWKS outage is reported as a 401 with error="invalid_token" rather than a 5xx; an OAuth client may re-run the login flow instead of backing off. Message tells the person to retry, and it is logged at Warn. Design choice, not a defect.
internal/httpapi/mcp.go:170 tools/list still advertises transit.* to an SSO principal whose ceiling is mcp:read; the call is refused with a clear scope message. Cosmetic.

mcpOAuthProvider caches a Provider per issuer forever (mutex held during discovery). Fine for a single issuer; a failed discovery is not cached so it retries per request, which is the intended behaviour.
